sound.verdict:
No blocker in the sound, but three things should be fixed before the client sees it: Luna's last line is 6-8 semitones lower than her first two (the voice fault class he rejected before), a squeal at 5.4 s is the loudest moment of the film, and the signature is missing on the very last frame. The last two are one-line edits; Luna needs a pitch fix or a retake. The rest measures clean: -14.0 LUFS, -2.0 dBTP, no clicks, no clipping, no digital silence, the drop's kick 10 ms after the cut, the final hit 21 ms after its cut, every line at least 6 dB over the music in the phone band.

I cannot hear. Resting on the listening model alone: whether voices sound like the same person, whether any line sounds synthetic, what the music resembles and whether it fits, and whether a loudness is comfortable. Its answers disagreed on Timo (4 of 5 say one man) and on which Luna line is the odd one; I have reported both as they came. Levels, pitch, timings and caption frames are measured. All 10 listening questions were used; nothing in the repository was changed.

picture.verdict: Not ready to show as it stands: one blocker and two majors, all in the picture and text. The blocker (the opening label blindfolds Luna for a second in her first close-up) and the vanishing signature on the last frame are caption retimes of minutes. The third, both scarves floating sideways in opposite directions at the gate, is in the clip and needs a new gate clip or a swap to take s7a_t2; the same shots also carry Luna's scarf turning teal-and-coral. The rest is minor and mostly edit work. The story itself reads from the picture alone, the cuts are clean, and the watch, backpack and jacket hold throughout.

3 of 6 (d, e, f) gave all seven elements. (a) gave 6 (no "he loves the suitcase"). (b) and (c) gave 5 (no passing the cat, no "he loves the suitcase"). Nobody got an element wrong, and all six followed the chain giant suitcase -> slow uphill push -> cat is faster -> ride down -> "it can't come in".

Per element, out of 6: her giant suitcase 6, slow uphill push 6, cat overtaking 6, riding down 6, passing the cat 4, he loves the suitcase 3, it cannot come in 6.

What the seven-element count hides: the intended retelling says "to the stadium", and only 1 of 6 named a stadium (b, whose role was told it follows football). 5 of 6 questioned the ending: c, d, e, f did not know why the suitcase cannot come in, (a) read it as not fitting through the gate, (b) understood a stadium rule but called it unrealistic.

- "He loves the suitcase" is legible, not lost in the picture or sound. The word reader gets "I love this suitcase" at 18.56-20.1 s in the mastered mix, the caption is up for 1.66 s, and both follow-up viewings described it correctly. It fell out of two-to-three-sentence retells.
- "Passing the cat" is on screen for 12 frames (14.96-15.42 s, measured), carried mostly by the cat's eye-pop and the caption "Too slow!". (b) and (c) remembered the cat only as the uphill gag.

viewers.verdict:
Not ready for the client as it stands, but both things that would trip a viewer are fixable by editing alone, with no new clips.

The plot now gets across: all six followed suitcase, uphill push, cat, ride down, "it can't come in", with nothing misread, and understanding averaged 8.2 of 10. The cat thread, which nobody understood last time, is understood by all six uphill and by four at the pay-off.

Two major problems remain:
- The ending does not land. The place is not read as a stadium (1 of 6, and that role was told it follows football), so "It can't come in, Timo" struck 5 of 6 as making no sense or as a plot hole. This is the one thing the client could call a screw-up. One caption label on the gate shot should fix it; re-test after.
- The uphill push at 4-7 s is where 4 of 6 would swipe. Nothing moves in frame, the cat stands still for the last 0.9 s, and the loudest voice sound in the film is a grunt at 5.25-5.75 s, 8-10 dB above the spoken lines. Trimming about 0.85 s and lowering that clip's sound fixes it.

Against the last proof: cat thread better, quiet music better, advert verdict the same (0 of 6 think a person posted it; the cause is now the 3D look and the VENUVOY chip), slow start not fixed.

Expect a cool reception even after the edits: enjoyment averaged 3.3 of 10, nobody would send it to a friend, and nobody would look for episode 2. The roles were told not to be polite, so treat those numbers as a harsh floor.

My claims about sound rest partly on the listening model. The level numbers, the word reader and the voice-similarity scores are measurements; that the grunt is annoying, that the music is audible enough, and that the meow goes unnoticed rest on the listening model alone.
